hero.title: New community center approved for Riverside after years of delay
hero.author: Sarah Chen
hero.content:
After nearly a decade of planning, delays, and community advocacy, the Riverside neighborhood will finally get its long-awaited community center. The city council voted 7-2 in favor of the project Tuesday evening, approving a $4.2 million budget to begin construction next spring.

The center, which will be located on the corner of Maple and 5th, will include a gymnasium, after-school tutoring rooms, a community kitchen, and outdoor recreation space. Local residents have been pushing for the facility since 2016, when the previous community building was demolished to make way for a parking structure.

'This is a huge win for our neighborhood,' said longtime resident and community organizer Diane Torres. 'Our kids have needed a safe space like this for years.'

Construction is expected to begin in March and wrap up by late 2027. The project will be funded through a combination of city bonds and a federal community development grant.

stack1.title: Mayor responds to housing affordability report with new task force
stack1.author: James Park
stack1.content:
Mayor Diane Collins announced the formation of a new Housing Affordability Task Force on Wednesday, responding to a damning report released last week that ranked the city among the least affordable in the region.

The task force will be composed of 12 members including city planners, housing advocates, developers, and tenant representatives. Their mandate is to produce a concrete action plan within 90 days.

'We cannot ignore these numbers,' Collins said at a press conference. 'Families are being priced out of the city they grew up in and that has to change.'

The report, published by the Regional Housing Coalition, found that median rent has increased 34% over the past five years while median income has grown just 9%.

stack2.title: UN security council convenes emergency session over ceasefire collapse
stack2.author: Reuters
stack2.content:
The United Nations Security Council convened an emergency session Wednesday after a fragile ceasefire agreement collapsed following a series of overnight strikes.

The session was called after reports emerged of renewed conflict in the contested border region, with both sides blaming the other for breaking the terms of the two-week-old truce.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged all parties to return to negotiations immediately, warning that a return to full-scale conflict would have devastating humanitarian consequences.

stack3.title: Researchers confirm new findings on deep-sea oxygen depletion trends
stack3.author: AP
stack3.content:
A new study published in the journal Nature Oceanography has confirmed accelerating oxygen depletion in deep-sea zones, a trend scientists say poses a significant threat to marine ecosystems worldwide.

Researchers from six universities analyzed data collected over 40 years and found that oxygen-minimum zones have expanded by an estimated 8% since the 1980s.

'This is not a distant threat — it is happening now,' said lead researcher Dr. Aiko Tanaka of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography.

latest1.title: District announces expanded after-school programs for fall semester
latest1.author: Maria Lopez
latest1.content:
The school district announced Wednesday that it will expand its after-school programming to eight additional schools starting this fall, bringing the total number of participating schools to 22.

The expansion is funded through a $1.1 million state grant and will offer tutoring, arts programs, and sports activities to an estimated 3,400 additional students.

latest2.title: Local high school soccer team advances to state championship finals
latest2.author: Sports Desk
latest2.content:
Jefferson High School's varsity soccer team punched their ticket to the state championship finals Tuesday night, defeating rival Westbrook Academy 3-1 in a tense semifinal match.

Senior forward Marcus Reid scored twice, including a stunning 25-yard strike in the 67th minute that sealed the game.

Jefferson will face Northside Prep in the championship game on Saturday at 2 p.m. at Memorial Stadium.

latest3.title: Study links microplastic exposure to measurable changes in lung tissue
latest3.author: Dr. Kim Nguyen
latest3.content:
A peer-reviewed study released Wednesday found measurable cellular changes in lung tissue samples from individuals with high levels of microplastic exposure.

The study analyzed tissue samples from 180 patients and found that those living near industrial zones had significantly higher concentrations of microplastic particles in their lung tissue.

The findings have been submitted to the EPA for review.

latest4.title: Free clinic expands evening hours to serve more uninsured residents
latest4.author: Dana Mills
latest4.content:
The Eastside Free Clinic announced this week that it will extend its operating hours to include Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 5 to 9 p.m.

The extended hours are expected to accommodate an additional 600 patients per year, funded through a private donation from a local family foundation.

No appointment is needed. Patients can walk in during clinic hours at 400 Eastside Boulevard.

latest5.title: Flooding across southern Europe displaces thousands ahead of winter
latest5.author: AP Wire
latest5.content:
Severe flooding across southern Europe has displaced an estimated 14,000 people this week as heavy rains overwhelmed river systems in Greece, Bulgaria, and northern Italy.

At least 11 fatalities have been confirmed across the three countries, with rescue operations still ongoing in several villages cut off by rising waters.

The European Union has activated its Civil Protection Mechanism to coordinate disaster relief.

latest6.title: Senate hearing on data privacy stalls over procedural disagreement
latest6.author: Raj Patel
latest6.content:
A Senate Commerce Committee hearing on federal data privacy legislation stalled Wednesday after members could not agree on the scope of testimony to be heard.

The disagreement centered on whether representatives from social media companies should be required to testify under oath.

The hearing has been rescheduled for next Tuesday.

world1.title: Ceasefire negotiations resume in Geneva as both sides agree to preliminary talks
world1.content:
Diplomatic representatives from both sides of the conflict arrived in Geneva Wednesday for preliminary ceasefire talks, marking the first direct negotiations in over three months.

Both delegations described the talks as 'constructive but difficult,' and agreed to return Thursday for a second round.

The talks come after intense diplomatic pressure from the United States and European Union.
world1.author: Reuters

world2.title: China's central bank cuts interest rates for the second time this quarter
world2.content:
The People's Bank of China announced Wednesday it would cut its benchmark lending rate by 0.25 percentage points, the second such reduction in three months.

The move signals that Chinese authorities are willing to use monetary policy aggressively to prop up growth, which came in below official targets in the most recent quarter.
world2.author: AP

world3.title: Brazil reports record Amazon deforestation drop following new enforcement push
world3.content:
Brazil's National Institute for Space Research reported Wednesday that Amazon deforestation fell to its lowest level in 15 years during the most recent monitoring period.

The data showed a 49% reduction in deforestation compared to the same period last year.

Brazil is set to host the COP30 climate summit next year, and officials say the deforestation data strengthens their credibility as a host nation.
world3.author: AFP

world4.title: Nigeria holds runoff elections amid reports of irregularities in three states
world4.content:
Nigerian voters returned to the polls Wednesday for gubernatorial runoff elections in four states, with international observers reporting irregularities including ballot shortages and polling station closures.

Opposition parties filed formal complaints in two states, alleging deliberate suppression of voter turnout.

Preliminary results are expected by Thursday evening.
world4.author: Al Jazeera

news1.title: City approves $12 million infrastructure plan for aging water pipes
news1.author: City Desk
news1.content:
The city council unanimously approved a $12 million plan Tuesday to replace aging water infrastructure across four neighborhoods.

Engineers flagged the pipes — some dating back to the 1940s — as a public health risk following two main breaks last winter.

Work is expected to begin in May and run through the end of the year, with temporary road closures affecting several major intersections.

news2.title: Public library launches free digital literacy classes for seniors
news2.author: Maria Lopez
news2.content:
The city's main public library branch will begin offering free weekly digital literacy workshops for adults over 60 starting next month.

The classes, funded through a state grant, will cover smartphone basics, online safety, video calling, and accessing government services online.

Registration opens Monday at the library's front desk or by calling the branch directly.

news3.title: Homeless shelter expansion gets final zoning approval after two-year fight
news3.author: Dana Mills
news3.content:
After more than two years of community debate and legal challenges, the city's largest homeless shelter has received final zoning approval to expand its capacity by 80 beds.

The expansion will bring the shelter's total capacity to 220, making it the largest facility of its kind in the region.

Construction is expected to take six months and will be funded through a combination of federal housing grants and private donations.

news4.title: New bus rapid transit line approved connecting downtown to airport
news4.author: Ben Okafor
news4.content:
The regional transit authority has approved a new bus rapid transit corridor that will connect downtown to the international airport in under 25 minutes.

The $38 million project will feature dedicated bus lanes, real-time tracking, and expanded park-and-ride facilities at three new stations.

Service is projected to launch in late 2027, with an estimated 8,000 daily riders in the first year of operation.

wcat1.title: G7 nations agree on new framework for AI regulation at summit
wcat1.content:
Leaders of the G7 nations reached a preliminary agreement Friday on a shared framework for regulating artificial intelligence, marking the first time major economies have coordinated on AI policy at the heads-of-government level.

The framework sets out common principles around transparency, accountability, and the protection of democratic institutions, though critics noted it lacks binding enforcement mechanisms.

The agreement will be submitted to each country's legislature for ratification over the coming months.

wcat2.title: South Korea and Japan announce historic joint defense agreement
wcat2.content:
South Korea and Japan signed a landmark joint defense cooperation agreement Saturday, the most significant bilateral security deal between the two countries in decades.

The pact establishes a framework for intelligence sharing, joint military exercises, and coordinated responses to regional threats.

The agreement comes amid heightened tensions on the Korean peninsula and growing concern over China's military activity in the South China Sea.

wcat3.title: WHO declares end to three-year mpox public health emergency
wcat3.content:
The World Health Organization officially declared an end to the global public health emergency for mpox on Thursday, citing a sustained decline in cases across all affected regions.

At its peak, the outbreak affected over 110 countries. The WHO credited widespread vaccination campaigns and improved surveillance systems for bringing the situation under control.

Officials cautioned that ongoing monitoring would continue, and that vaccination programs in high-risk areas would be maintained.

wcat4.title: Arctic ice coverage hits second-lowest recorded level this winter
wcat4.content:
Arctic sea ice coverage reached its second-lowest extent on record this past winter, according to data released by the National Snow and Ice Data Center.

Scientists said the findings are consistent with long-term warming trends and represent a significant concern for ecosystems and communities that depend on stable ice conditions.

The record low was set in 2012. Researchers say current trajectories suggest summer ice-free conditions in the Arctic could occur within two decades.

pol1.title: Governor signs landmark clean energy bill into law
pol1.author: Raj Patel
pol1.content:
The governor signed a sweeping clean energy bill into law Wednesday that commits the state to generating 100% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2040.

The bill passed the legislature on a largely party-line vote after months of negotiation over provisions affecting the fossil fuel industry and rural energy ratepayers.

Environmental groups called it a historic victory, while business associations warned of potential rate increases for consumers and manufacturers.

pol2.title: Congressional redistricting battle heads to federal court
pol2.author: James Park
pol2.content:
A federal lawsuit challenging the state's newly drawn congressional district maps will proceed to trial after a judge denied a motion to dismiss on Thursday.

Plaintiffs argue the maps constitute an unconstitutional partisan gerrymander that effectively dilutes the voting power of minority communities in three districts.

The case is expected to go to trial in June, with a potential appeal to the Supreme Court regardless of the outcome.

pol3.title: City ethics board opens investigation into planning department contracts
pol3.author: City Desk
pol3.content:
The city's independent ethics board announced Thursday it has opened a formal investigation into contracting practices within the planning department following complaints from two former employees.

The investigation focuses on whether proper bidding procedures were followed on four contracts awarded over the past three years totaling approximately $2.1 million.

The planning department said it would cooperate fully with the investigation and has placed two senior staff members on administrative leave pending the outcome.

pol4.title: School board election draws record number of candidates amid curriculum debate
pol4.author: Maria Lopez
pol4.content:
This year's school board election has attracted 23 candidates for five open seats — the highest number in the district's recorded history — as debates over curriculum, book policies, and school funding have intensified.

Candidates span a wide range of platforms, from those calling for expanded arts and vocational programs to others focused on restricting certain classroom materials.

Voter registration for the May election closes April 28.

sp1.title: City FC signs former Premier League striker ahead of new season
sp1.author: Sports Desk
sp1.content:
City FC announced the signing of former Premier League striker Dayo Adeyemi on a two-year deal Wednesday, the club's most high-profile acquisition in years.

Adeyemi, 28, scored 14 goals in 31 appearances for Burnley last season before his contract expired. He is expected to start in Saturday's opening match of the regional league season.

'I'm here to win,' Adeyemi said at his introductory press conference. 'This club has real ambition and I want to be part of it.'

sp2.title: High school basketball star commits to Division I program
sp2.author: Sports Desk
sp2.content:
Jefferson High senior point guard Keisha Daniels announced her commitment to the University of Connecticut women's basketball program on Wednesday, choosing UConn over offers from seven other Division I schools.

Daniels averaged 24.3 points and 8.1 assists per game this season, leading Jefferson to its first state championship in 11 years.

She is considered one of the top-10 high school prospects in the country by multiple recruiting services.

sp3.title: Local marathon draws record 12,000 runners from 40 countries
sp3.author: Dana Mills
sp3.content:
This year's annual city marathon drew a record 12,000 registered runners from 40 countries, organizers confirmed Wednesday, up from 9,400 participants last year.

Kenyan runner Abebe Girma won the men's race in 2:07:44, just 18 seconds off the course record. Ethiopian Tigist Assefa won the women's race in 2:19:08, setting a new course record.

The event generated an estimated $4.2 million in economic activity for the city, according to the chamber of commerce.

sp4.title: Minor league baseball team announces new downtown stadium plans
sp4.author: Ben Okafor
sp4.content:
The River Cats minor league baseball team unveiled plans Wednesday for a new 7,500-seat downtown stadium, pending approval from the city council.

The $42 million facility would replace the team's current 40-year-old stadium and include upgraded amenities, a public plaza, and year-round event space.

The team has requested a 30-year lease on city-owned land near the waterfront. A council vote is expected in June.

h1.title: New study finds Mediterranean diet reduces dementia risk by 23%
h1.author: Dr. Kim Nguyen
h1.content:
A large-scale study published in the New England Journal of Medicine has found that consistent adherence to a Mediterranean diet is associated with a 23% reduction in dementia risk over a 10-year follow-up period.

The study tracked 60,000 adults across 12 countries and controlled for factors including age, physical activity, smoking, and cardiovascular health.

Researchers cautioned that the findings show association rather than causation, and that diet is one of many factors influencing cognitive health.

h2.title: County health department expands free mental health hotline hours
h2.author: Dana Mills
h2.content:
The county health department announced Wednesday it will extend its free mental health support hotline to 24-hour availability starting May 1, up from the current 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. schedule.

The expansion is funded through a federal behavioral health grant and will add 14 full-time and part-time counselor positions.

Residents can reach the hotline at the existing number. Spanish-language support will also be available around the clock under the new schedule.

h3.title: FDA approves first at-home test for early-stage colon cancer detection
h3.author: AP Wire
h3.content:
The Food and Drug Administration on Thursday approved the first over-the-counter test capable of detecting early-stage colorectal cancer biomarkers at home, a development health experts say could significantly increase screening rates.

The test, developed by a Massachusetts biotech firm, uses a stool sample and returns results within 30 minutes. It will be available at major pharmacies for an estimated retail price of $49.

Colorectal cancer is the second-leading cause of cancer death in the United States, and early detection dramatically improves survival outcomes.

h4.title: Hospital system launches mobile clinic to reach underserved rural areas
h4.author: Maria Lopez
h4.content:
Regional Medical Center announced Thursday it will deploy two fully equipped mobile medical clinics to serve rural communities within a 60-mile radius of the city, beginning this summer.

The clinics will offer primary care visits, preventive screenings, vaccinations, and chronic disease management on a rotating weekly schedule across eight communities.

The initiative is funded through a five-year, $3.8 million federal rural health grant and is expected to serve approximately 4,500 patients annually.

sc1.title: NASA confirms water ice deposits discovered in permanently shadowed lunar craters
sc1.author: AP
sc1.content:
NASA scientists confirmed Thursday the presence of substantial water ice deposits in permanently shadowed craters near the Moon's south pole, based on new data from the LCROSS and LRO missions.

The discovery significantly strengthens the case for establishing a sustainable lunar base, as water ice can be converted into drinking water, oxygen, and rocket fuel.

The findings, published in the journal Nature Geoscience, show ice concentrations higher than previously estimated in at least six crater locations.

sc2.title: Breakthrough in solid-state battery technology could double EV range
sc2.author: Reuters
sc2.content:
Researchers at MIT have announced a breakthrough in solid-state battery technology that could more than double the range of electric vehicles while significantly reducing charging times.

The new battery design replaces the liquid electrolyte used in conventional lithium-ion batteries with a solid ceramic material, improving both energy density and safety.

The team estimates the technology could reach commercial production within five to seven years, pending further testing and manufacturing scale-up.

sc3.title: Scientists sequence genome of 52,000-year-old woolly mammoth for first time
sc3.author: AFP
sc3.content:
An international team of scientists has successfully sequenced the complete genome of a woolly mammoth preserved in Siberian permafrost for approximately 52,000 years, the oldest intact mammalian genome ever decoded.

The research, published in Cell, reveals new details about mammoth population decline and their genetic relationship to modern Asian elephants.

The findings also contribute to ongoing efforts to use gene-editing technology to restore mammoth traits in elephant cell lines, a project that remains years from any practical application.

sc4.title: Webb telescope captures clearest images yet of exoplanet atmosphere
sc4.author: NASA
sc4.content:
The James Webb Space Telescope has produced the most detailed observations ever recorded of an exoplanet atmosphere, detecting carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor in the atmosphere of a planet 120 light-years from Earth.

The planet, K2-18b, orbits within its star's habitable zone and has a mass roughly 8.6 times that of Earth, placing it in the 'sub-Neptune' category.

While scientists caution that the findings do not indicate the presence of life, the chemical signatures detected are consistent with conditions that could theoretically support biological activity.

npr_105c3546.title: Some plants have unusual genetics, which can help them weather cataclysmic events
npr_105c3546.author: NPR
npr_105c3546.content:
Many plants have more than two sets of chromosomes, a trait that is uncommon in humans. This genetic characteristic can be beneficial for plants in certain situations.

Having extra sets of chromosomes allows plants to adapt more easily to environmental changes. This can be particularly useful in the face of significant upheaval, such as climate change. The additional chromosomes provide plants with a greater range of genetic material, which can help them survive and thrive in changing conditions.

The ability of plants to withstand environmental stress is closely tied to their genetic makeup. Plants with multiple sets of chromosomes may be better equipped to handle extreme weather events and other disruptions. This is because their extra chromosomes provide a buffer against genetic damage and mutation.

This genetic trait is found in many plant species, and it may play a key role in their ability to survive and adapt to changing environments.

bbc_99dcaae6.title: 'We're right on track,' says Streeting as key target for hospital waiting times hit
bbc_99dcaae6.author: BBC News
bbc_99dcaae6.content:
The government has met its interim target for hospital waiting times in England. As of the latest available data, 65% of patients are being treated within 18 weeks.

This target is part of a broader effort to reduce waiting times for medical treatment. The government had set a goal to achieve this milestone, and according to the latest numbers, it has been reached.

A government representative has confirmed that the target has been met, stating that progress is on track. The achievement of this target indicates that a significant proportion of patients in England are receiving timely medical attention.

The target applies to patients waiting for treatment in England's hospitals. The data shows that 65% of these patients are currently being treated within the 18-week timeframe.

bbc_a9b01e64.title: 'Don't swim' at 12 of 14 river bathing sites, as more locations announced
bbc_a9b01e64.author: BBC News
bbc_a9b01e64.content:
Twelve out of 14 designated river bathing sites in England have been found to have high levels of bacteria linked to faeces. As a result, warnings against swimming have been issued for these locations.

The bacteria levels exceeded safe limits, prompting the warnings. The designated river bathing sites are monitored for water quality to ensure they are safe for public use.

Only two of the 14 sites had acceptable bacteria levels. The remaining 12 sites had levels that were too high, making them unsuitable for swimming.

The affected locations have been identified and warnings have been issued to inform the public of the potential health risks associated with swimming in these areas.

bbc_ef75e094.title: White-tailed eagles to be released in Exmoor despite farmer warnings
bbc_ef75e094.author: BBC News
bbc_ef75e094.content:
A reintroduction program for white-tailed eagles is set to take place in Exmoor. The white-tailed eagle is the UK's largest bird of prey.

Some farmers in the area have expressed concerns about the program, citing potential threats to their livestock. They have warned that the eagles may attack and kill their animals.

The white-tailed eagle is a large bird, and its presence can have an impact on local wildlife and farming practices. The eagles are known to prey on small and medium-sized animals.

The reintroduction program is moving forward, with the eagles set to be released in Exmoor. Further details about the program and its potential effects on local farming and wildlife are not available at this time.

npr_a4164320.title: Colorado's Democratic governor will let Trump ally Tina Peters out of prison early
npr_a4164320.author: NPR
npr_a4164320.content:
Colorado Governor Jared Polis has commuted the sentence of Tina Peters, a former county official. Peters was convicted of tampering with election equipment.

Peters' conviction stemmed from her actions as a county official. The commutation means she will be released from prison early. 

The decision to commute Peters' sentence follows a campaign by the Trump administration to secure her release. The Trump administration had pushed for Peters to be freed.

Governor Polis' commutation of Peters' sentence is now in effect, allowing for her early release from prison.

guardian_12681967.title: Listen and learn: the hidden secret to spotting a liar
guardian_12681967.author: The Guardian
guardian_12681967.content:
Research has identified a method to improve one's ability to detect deception. This technique involves closing one's eyes while interacting with the person suspected of lying.

Closing one's eyes can reportedly double a person's chances of accurately identifying dishonesty. This approach has been found to be effective even when other methods, including artificial intelligence, have failed.

The technique's effectiveness has also been noted in the context of game shows, where contestants have attempted to deceive each other. Despite the use of various strategies, many participants have been unable to successfully detect lies.

This method of detecting deception is based on the idea that visual cues can sometimes be misleading or distracting. By eliminating visual information, individuals may be able to focus more accurately on other indicators of dishonesty, such as tone of voice or speech patterns.

guardian_7886434b.title: ‘It makes me feel quite dehumanised’: young at London career fair lay bare barriers to jobs
guardian_7886434b.author: The Guardian
guardian_7886434b.content:
A career fair was held at Westfield White City, the largest shopping mall in the UK, where hundreds of young people attended in search of job opportunities. The event, which takes place annually, features a range of employers, including the Metropolitan police and car valet services.

The job fair is particularly relevant this year due to high unemployment levels, with young people being disproportionately affected. The UK capital is often seen as a hub for work opportunities, but many young people are struggling to find employment.

The event drew a large crowd, with many attendees seeking to find job opportunities in various fields. The career fair provides a platform for young people to connect with potential employers and learn about available job openings.

The high levels of youth unemployment have raised concerns about the challenges faced by young people in the job market. The career fair aims to address these challenges by bringing together employers and job seekers in one place.

bbc_a5bc2d0c.title: Trump and Xi conclude 'very successful' talks but few deals confirmed
bbc_a5bc2d0c.author: BBC News
bbc_a5bc2d0c.content:
A two-day meeting between US and Chinese leaders has concluded. The meeting included various ceremonies and events.

The leaders described the talks as "very successful". However, few specific agreements or deals were announced as a result of the discussions.

The visit was intended to address trade issues between the two countries. Despite the lack of concrete trade breakthroughs, the tone of the meeting was reportedly positive.

The outcome of the meeting was largely ceremonial, with no major announcements or policy changes confirmed. The leaders' characterization of the talks as successful suggests a positive atmosphere, but details of any future cooperation or agreements remain unclear.

guardian_eb0e3175.title: Judge orders Trump administration to return Colombian woman deported to DRC back to the US
guardian_eb0e3175.author: The Guardian
guardian_eb0e3175.content:
A federal judge has ordered the government to return a Colombian woman to the US from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The woman, Adriana Maria Quiroz Zapata, was deported to the African country, which had previously refused to accept her.

The judge's ruling stated that Quiroz Zapata's deportation was "likely illegal". The decision was made by US district judge Richard Leon on Wednesday.

Quiroz Zapata is to be returned to the US. The details of her deportation and the circumstances surrounding her case have been noted in the judge's ruling.

The order to return Quiroz Zapata to the US has been issued, with the judge's decision citing the likely illegality of her deportation.

bbc_a0050d81.title: British firm vying to build next Red Arrows jets collapses
bbc_a0050d81.author: BBC News
bbc_a0050d81.content:
A British firm that was seeking to build the next generation of Red Arrows jets has collapsed. The company, Aeralis, was hoping to secure a contract from the UK government to replace the Hawk jets currently used by the Royal Air Force.

The Hawk jets are currently flown by the Red Arrows, the RAF's aerobatic team. Aeralis had been in the running to provide the replacement jets, but the company's collapse has put its bid in jeopardy.

The UK government had been considering Aeralis' proposal as part of its plans to replace the existing Hawk jets. The government's decision on the contract had not been announced prior to the company's collapse.

The collapse of Aeralis may impact the UK government's plans for replacing the Hawk jets. The government's next steps on the contract are not yet clear.

guardian_fdad9ca0.title: Andy Burnham will push to become PM before Labour conference, allies say
guardian_fdad9ca0.author: The Guardian
guardian_fdad9ca0.content:
Andy Burnham will attempt to become Prime Minister before the Labour party conference, according to his supporters. The conference is scheduled to take place in Liverpool this autumn.

The Greater Manchester mayor has been given permission by Labour's ruling body to stand for the Makerfield seat in an upcoming byelection. This is the first step in his bid to become a candidate.

The byelection is expected to be contested by Reform UK, who plan to put up a strong fight. 

The Labour party conference in Liverpool is being targeted as a potential venue for Burnham to make a significant appearance, should he be successful in his bid to become the party's candidate.

nasa_04d9ef39.title: NASA Science, Cargo Launch on 34th SpaceX Resupply Mission to Station
nasa_04d9ef39.author: NASA
nasa_04d9ef39.content:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launched from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Friday at 6:05 p.m. EDT. The launch marked the 34th SpaceX commercial resupply mission under contract with NASA.

The mission is headed to the International Space Station, carrying new scientific experiments. The spacecraft is loaded with nearly 6,500 pounds of cargo.

The launch is part of an ongoing effort to resupply the International Space Station. The spacecraft will deliver its cargo to the station, supporting ongoing research and operations.

The spacecraft was launched on a Falcon 9 rocket, which lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The launch occurred on Friday at 6:05 p.m. EDT.

bbc_df443ac7.title: MPs call for sunbed advertising ban to help prevent skin cancer
bbc_df443ac7.author: BBC News
bbc_df443ac7.content:
A cross-party group of MPs has released a report on skin cancer prevention. The report found that most skin cancer cases can be prevented.

The MPs are calling for a ban on sunbed advertising as part of their efforts to prevent skin cancer. This recommendation is based on the report's findings.

The report states that the majority of skin cancer cases are preventable. The MPs' goal is to reduce the number of skin cancer cases through preventative measures.

The report's findings and recommendations will be considered as part of ongoing efforts to address skin cancer.

guardian_84841fd4.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power
guardian_84841fd4.author: The Guardian
guardian_84841fd4.content:
Mali's armed forces, supported by Russian mercenaries, have launched airstrikes against a rebel alliance. The alliance consists of Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists.

The airstrikes come after the rebel alliance launched a surprise offensive across much of Mali in late April. The offensive resulted in the loss of the key northern town of Kidal.

Warplanes targeted Kidal earlier this week. The town is a significant location in the conflict. The ruling junta is working to maintain its hold on power in the unstable west African country.

The situation in Mali remains volatile, with the junta struggling to maintain control. The conflict involves various groups, including Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists, as well as the armed forces and their Russian mercenary supporters.

guardian_510f4f0e.title: Nymphomaniacs and sex droughts: what I learned while studying women’s pleasure
guardian_510f4f0e.author: The Guardian
guardian_510f4f0e.content:
Historical records indicate that in ancient times, women were considered to be more sexual than men. However, this perception has changed over time. 

In recent years, there has been a reported decline in the frequency of sex in several countries, including Britain, the US, France, and Australia. Denmark is an exception to this trend. 

This decline has been noted in various publications, with some referring to it as a "sex recession." The topic has been discussed in several articles, including ones published in 2018 and last December. 

These articles have referenced ancient historical periods, suggesting that sex was more plentiful in the past. However, historical records show that ancient times were not a period of sexual freedom, particularly for women.

bbc_515f0c05.title: Burnham cleared to run for selection in pivotal by-election
bbc_515f0c05.author: BBC News
bbc_515f0c05.content:
The mayor of Greater Manchester has been cleared to run for selection in an upcoming by-election. This development could potentially have significant implications for national politics.

If the mayor wins the by-election, they would be eligible to launch a leadership challenge against the Prime Minister. The by-election is considered pivotal, and the outcome may have far-reaching consequences.

The mayor's candidacy has been given the green light, allowing them to proceed with their bid for selection. The next steps in the process will determine whether they will be selected as a candidate in the by-election.

The outcome of the by-election and the mayor's potential candidacy are being closely watched, as they may impact the national political landscape. Further developments are expected in the coming days.

guardian_9f0f1a68.title: Ice vests or daily cold showers could help people lose weight, study finds
guardian_9f0f1a68.author: The Guardian
guardian_9f0f1a68.content:
Researchers have found that daily exposure to cold temperatures can help people lose weight. A study of 47 adults with obesity or overweight showed that regular cold exposure led to fat loss. 

The study found that cold temperatures activate brown fat, which can help speed up the body's burning of calories. 

Participants in the study wore ice vests or took daily cold showers as part of the research. The results suggest that these methods of cold exposure could be used to aid in weight loss. 

The study's findings provide new data on the health benefits of cold exposure, an area that has had minimal research to date.

npr_381d02a2.title: The Supreme Court keeps abortion pill mifepristone available by telehealth
npr_381d02a2.author: NPR
npr_381d02a2.content:
The Supreme Court has ruled that the abortion pill mifepristone can continue to be prescribed online or over the phone. This means that patients can receive prescriptions for the medication remotely, without having to visit a doctor in person.

The court's decision allows mifepristone to be sent through the mail to patients who have received a prescription. This method of distribution has been permitted during the COVID-19 pandemic and will continue to be allowed.

The ruling was made on Thursday and applies to the availability of mifepristone via telehealth services. Telehealth services provide medical care remotely, often through online platforms or phone calls.

The decision ensures that patients can continue to access mifepristone through remote means, rather than being required to visit a doctor's office or clinic in person to obtain a prescription.

guardian_3654e6fd.title: Far-right activists barred from UK before Tommy Robinson rally
guardian_3654e6fd.author: The Guardian
guardian_3654e6fd.content:
Eleven foreign far-right activists have been blocked from entering the UK. This action was taken before a rally by supporters of Tommy Robinson, which took place on Saturday.

The rally was the second of its kind, following an event last year that drew over 100,000 attendees. Ahead of the rally, Keir Starmer accused Tommy Robinson of "peddling hatred and division".

The archbishop of Canterbury urged people to "choose hope" before the event. Other faith leaders also spoke out against the rally.

The actions of the authorities and the statements from public figures came as the UK prepared for the rally, which was expected to draw a large crowd.

npr_05dceb37.title: Researchers unearth Southeast Asia's largest dinosaur
npr_05dceb37.author: NPR
npr_05dceb37.content:
Researchers have discovered a dinosaur in Southeast Asia that is the largest found in the region. The dinosaur is a sauropod, a type of herbivore with a long neck and tail.

The dinosaur is estimated to have lived during the late Early Cretaceous period, around 100 to 120 million years ago. This time period is significant in the history of dinosaur evolution.

The discovery of this dinosaur provides new information about the prehistoric animals that lived in Southeast Asia. The dinosaur's size makes it a notable find in the region.

Further details about the discovery and the dinosaur's characteristics are not available at this time. The dinosaur has been referred to as the "last titan" of Thailand, due to its large size and the country where it was found.

The operation resulted in the elimination of al-Minuki. No further details about the operation have been released.

The US president made the announcement, confirming the death of the senior IS leader. The joint operation involved cooperation between US and Nigerian forces, leading to the successful elimination of the target.

The recorded conversation with Figueroa and his mother is part of a collection of stories from individuals and their families. These stories provide a glimpse into the lives and experiences of people from various backgrounds.

nasa_5b990ad8.title: Hubble Sights Galaxy in Transition
nasa_5b990ad8.author: NASA
nasa_5b990ad8.content:
The NASA Hubble Space Telescope has captured an image of a galaxy with a bright center. The galaxy's face suggests a spiral structure, but it does not have obvious spiral arms. 

 
The image shows reddish-brown clumps and filaments of dust that partially obscure the galaxy's face. Light from distant galaxies can be seen shining through the outer regions of the galaxy.

 
The galaxy's outer regions are diffuse, allowing light from other galaxies to be visible. The image shows a combination of red, blue, and orange light from these distant galaxies.

 
The Hubble Space Telescope image provides a detailed view of the galaxy's structure and composition. The image reveals the galaxy's complex appearance, with dust and light from other galaxies visible throughout.

guardian_bb2ce9b1.title: A third of Britons believe they have changed social class, survey finds
guardian_bb2ce9b1.author: The Guardian
guardian_bb2ce9b1.content:
A recent survey found that over a third of Britons believe they have changed social class. The survey also identified a group of around 6 million people, referred to as the "polyclass," who consider themselves to belong to more than one social category.

Upper-middle and upper-class individuals were most likely to identify with multiple classes. In contrast, working-class people were the least likely to report a change in social class or identify with more than one class.

According to the survey, 70% of working-class individuals stated that they were in the same social category they were born into. This suggests that working-class people may be less likely to experience social mobility or identify with multiple classes.

The survey's findings provide insight into the complexities of social class in Britain, highlighting the diversity of experiences and identities within the population.

bbc_e035bebe.title: Posh sandwich has more salt than nearly five cheeseburgers
bbc_e035bebe.author: BBC News
bbc_e035bebe.content:
A recent study found that a particular type of posh sandwich contains high levels of salt. The amount of salt in this sandwich is comparable to nearly five cheeseburgers.

The organization that conducted the study, which focuses on salt and sugar content in food, reported the findings. They noted that consumers may be unaware of the high salt content in certain lunch options.

The group warned that people should be aware of the potential health risks associated with consuming high amounts of salt. They stated that buying lunch should not expose individuals to hidden health risks.

The study highlights the need for consumers to be informed about the salt content in the food they purchase. It provides information that can help people make more informed decisions about their diet and health.

npr_48061f1c.title: Elephants eat their crops. Farmers strike back. It's a war that's only getting worse
npr_48061f1c.author: NPR
npr_48061f1c.content:

Farmers are taking action in response to the elephants eating their crops. The conflict is causing problems for both the farmers and the elephants, with no clear solution in sight.

The elephants are generally revered by the people of Sri Lanka, but the conflict with farmers is causing rising tensions. The situation continues to escalate, with both sides suffering losses.

npr_6a35a92c.title: Hantavirus countdown: U.S. cruise passengers settle in for 42 days of waiting

Some passengers may be cleared to quarantine at home instead of in Nebraska. The decision to allow home quarantine will be made on a case-by-case basis.

The quarantine period of 42 days is intended to ensure that any potential cases of hantavirus are identified and contained. The passengers will be monitored during this time for any symptoms of the disease.

npr_a55e111a.title: North America poised for light display of aurora borealis
npr_a55e111a.author: NPR

The aurora borealis, also known as the northern lights, is expected to be visible in North America. This natural light display occurs at night and is caused by charged particles from the sun interacting with the Earth's magnetic field.

The best time to observe the aurora borealis is predicted to be on Saturday and Sunday nights. 

The display is expected to be a light show, and viewers can look forward to seeing it in the night sky on the specified days.

Viewers in North America can look to the sky on Saturday and Sunday nights for a chance to see the aurora borealis.

guardian_5e0088da.title: British Palestinians feel ‘gaslit’ and unable to speak out, says leading activist

The Nakba march is scheduled to take place, with Husseini's comments highlighting the concerns and fears of British Palestinians in the lead-up to the event.

npr_bf5e7989.author: NPR

A humpback whale was found dead off the coast of a Danish island. The whale has been identified as the one released two weeks ago after a rescue effort. The rescue took place after the whale became stranded multiple times off the coast of Germany's Baltic Sea.

The whale, named Timmy, was the subject of a notable rescue operation. It had become stranded off Germany's Baltic Sea coast on several occasions before being released.

Danish authorities confirmed the identification of the whale on Saturday. The whale was found dead off the coast of a Danish island earlier in the week.

The whale's release had taken place two weeks prior to its discovery. It had been rescued after becoming stranded off Germany's Baltic Sea coast multiple times.

nasa_60668334.title: Curiosity Shakes Loose a Pesky Rock
nasa_60668334.author: NASA
nasa_60668334.content:
NASA's Curiosity Mars rover drilled a sample from a rock on April 25, 2026. After withdrawing its robotic arm, the rover pulled the entire rock off the surface with it.

The rock remained attached to the rover's arm for several days. Engineers attempted to dislodge it by repositioning the arm and vibrating the drill.

These efforts continued until May 1, when the rock finally detached from the rover's arm. The incident occurred after the rover had successfully drilled a sample from the rock.

The rock's detachment on May 1 ended the incident, which had begun when the rover drilled the sample on April 25.

bbc_10925ff3.content:
A Canadian who was a passenger on the MV Hondius cruise ship has tested positive for hantavirus. The individual is currently isolating on Vancouver Island, British Columbia.

The person is one of four former passengers from the ship who are isolating on the island. All four individuals were on the MV Hondius, which has been linked to cases of hantavirus.

Hantavirus is a viral disease that can be transmitted to humans through contact with infected rodents or their droppings. The virus can cause severe illness in humans, including respiratory and kidney problems.

npr_56a203cd.title: Napoleon Solo holds off Iron Honor to win the Preakness
npr_56a203cd.author: NPR
npr_56a203cd.content:
Napoleon Solo has won the Preakness, earning the colt's first victory of the year. The field of 14 horses was considered wide open due to the absence of Kentucky Derby winner Golden Tempo.

Napoleon Solo held off Iron Honor to take the win. The Preakness is the middle jewel of the Triple Crown.

The absence of Golden Tempo, the Kentucky Derby winner, had left the field without a clear favorite. This created an opportunity for other horses to compete for the top spot.

Napoleon Solo's win marks a significant achievement for the colt, being its first victory this year. The outcome of the race will be followed by further events in the Triple Crown series.

guardian_239117e6.title: Prostate cancer screening can save lives but ‘absolute benefit is small’, study says
guardian_239117e6.author: The Guardian
guardian_239117e6.content:
A recent study analyzed six trials involving nearly 800,000 men to assess the effectiveness of prostate cancer screening. The study found that screening with a blood test can reduce deaths from prostate cancer.

The blood test, which measures prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels, was shown to reduce prostate cancer deaths by two for every 1,000 men screened. This means that 500 men must be screened to prevent one death from the disease.

The study's findings also indicate that many men may face unnecessary treatment and medical complications as a result of screening. 

The study's results are based on a comprehensive review of existing data and provide insight into the benefits and potential drawbacks of prostate cancer screening.

guardian_b8983d63.title: Fire and ‘sheer volume’: how Britain’s 6m-vape problem is putting recycling under strain
guardian_b8983d63.author: The Guardian
guardian_b8983d63.content:
A recycling plant near Birmingham city centre is handling a large number of discarded vape devices. A site operative, Ana, sorts and dismantles the devices as part of her job. She processes about half a bucket of vapes per shift, with each bucket containing between 40 and 50 devices.

The recycling process for vapes is not simple. Ana uses a hammer to smash each device open and then separates the components into different containers. This includes removing the batteries from each vape.

Waste professionals say that the disposal of vape devices is a significant issue, with an estimated 6 million devices discarded each year. This is reported to cost £1 billion annually.

The issue persists despite a ban on disposable vapes. Recycling plants like the one near Birmingham city centre continue to handle large quantities of discarded devices, with site operatives like Ana working to process them.
